claims.text: The starting material is the HfZrTiTa0.53 refractory high-entropy alloy.
The starting alloy is in an as-cast, single-phase condition.
The alloy has a quasi-static yield strength of 786 MPa.
The alloy has a quasi-static compressive strength of 1314 MPa.
The alloy has a quasi-static fracture strain of 13.5%.
A targeted heat treatment can nucleate and grow a fine, homogeneously distributed nanoscale secondary BCC precipitate phase in HfZrTiTa0.53.
The proposed precipitates will obstruct dislocation motion.
The proposed precipitates will provide sites for dislocation pile-up.
Precipitate-dislocation interactions will increase work hardening.
Increased work hardening will delay the transition from uniform deformation to localized deformation.
The precipitate-mediated interactions will increase the energy required to nucleate shear bands at high strain rates.
Relative to an as-cast control tested dynamically, the heat-treated alloy will have higher dynamic yield strength.
Relative to an as-cast control tested dynamically, the heat-treated alloy will exhibit a greater strain-hardening response.
Relative to an as-cast control tested dynamically, the heat-treated alloy will sustain more uniform deformation and delay localization.
Relative to an as-cast control tested dynamically, the heat-treated alloy will have a higher fracture strain before failure.
Relative to an as-cast control tested dynamically, the heat-treated alloy will absorb more impact-induced energy.
The prediction is intended to apply under adiabatic dynamic deformation at strain rates above 1000 s^-1.
The benefits may be reduced or different under lower-strain-rate or isothermal loading.
